# MASTER VIDEO PRODUCTION PROMPT — the only authoritative template

**Status: PERMANENT SYSTEM FILE.** Every new video starts by copying this template into
`projects/<slug>/PROMPT.md`, customising every `{{...}}` slot with that video's own research, and
**saving the finalised prompt before production begins**. Do not edit this file for one video's
benefit: if a production exposes a missing instruction, improve this template and record it in
[`CHANGELOG.md`](../CHANGELOG.md) and
[`docs/production/PIPELINE_CHANGELOG.md`](../docs/production/PIPELINE_CHANGELOG.md).

Governing rules: [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md) · Primary procedure:
[`skills/animation-production/SKILL.md`](../skills/animation-production/SKILL.md) · Specialist
skills: [`skills/README.md`](../skills/README.md) · Machinery:
[`universal_toolbook/README.md`](../universal_toolbook/README.md) · Project checklist:
[`templates/VIDEO_PROJECT_TEMPLATE/PROJECT_FILES.md`](VIDEO_PROJECT_TEMPLATE/PROJECT_FILES.md) ·
Worked examples: [`projects/video-001-twenty-three-minutes/PROMPT.md`](../projects/video-001-twenty-three-minutes/PROMPT.md)
and [`projects/video-002-discipline-vs-obsession/PROMPT.md`](../projects/video-002-discipline-vs-obsession/PROMPT.md).

This template is the **per-video creative brief**, not a second copy of the production procedure.
Stage-by-stage execution lives in the skills; detailed stage documentation lives in
[`docs/production/INDEX.md`](../docs/production/INDEX.md).

---

## 0. Mission

Produce one complete, watchable, production-ready MP4 {{FORMAT_LINE, e.g. "stickman animation as a
YouTube Short (1080×1920, 9:16, ≤180 s)"}} from research through render and QA, in a new
independent project folder, using the reusable pipeline. The deliverable is a **video file** — not
a plan, a script, a still or a report. Do not stop at recommendations.

- **Project folder:** `projects/{{SLUG}}/`
- **Prompt saved before production:** `PROMPT.md` (this file, fully customised)
- **Required skills:** animation-production + scriptwriting, stickman-animation, voiceover-audio,
  youtube-research (where appropriate), production-quality
- **Primary CLI:** `python3 universal_toolbook/run_studio.py …`
- **Ordered gates:** `python3 tools/produce_video.py projects/{{SLUG}}`

## 1. Selected topic

- **Title:** {{TITLE}}
- **Premise:** {{ONE_PARAGRAPH_PREMISE}}
- **Thesis (one sentence):** {{THESIS}}
- **Target runtime / format:** {{TARGET_RUNTIME}} · {{ASPECT_AND_RESOLUTION}}
- **Selection rationale:** see `TOPIC_SELECTION.md`
- **Evidence:** see `RESEARCH.md` (sources, dates, `[M]` measured / `[O]` observed / `[P]` predicted)

## 2. Research constraints on the script

- {{FACT_1}} — confidence {{HIGH|MEDIUM-HIGH|MEDIUM}} → {{MAY/MAY NOT}} be asserted in narration.
- {{FACT_2}} — confidence {{...}} → {{...}}
- {{HYPOTHESIS}} is an explicit thought experiment and must be introduced as one, not as a
  measured quantity.
- Every number asserted in narration must trace to a High or Medium-High confidence row in
  `RESEARCH.md` §5. Medium-confidence figures stay out. Never call a topic viral on a guess.
- Research procedure: [`skills/youtube-research/SKILL.md`](../skills/youtube-research/SKILL.md)
  and [`docs/production/IDEA_RESEARCH.md`](../docs/production/IDEA_RESEARCH.md).

## 3. Creative direction

1. Runtime {{TARGET_RUNTIME}}; beats of 10–20 s; hook inside the first 10 seconds.
2. **One metaphor, carried to exhaustion, never explained:** {{METAPHOR}}.
3. Narration register {{REGISTER}}; no lecturing; show rather than tell.
4. Where the argument allows, prove it by showing the same conditions with one variable changed.
5. **Mute-legibility:** the film must be understandable with the audio off.
6. Close on an originally worded direct-address question {{UNLESS_SUPPLIED_SCRIPT_OVERRIDES}}.
7. Music is load-bearing, shifts mood per act and is ducked under narration.
8. Chapter labels double as on-screen cards and as YouTube chapters.
9. **Originality:** no character, script, scene, chapter list or metaphor reproduced from a
   reference; references inform craft only.
10. English narration, no channel name, watermark or channel branding.

## 3a. Creative strategy — decide before writing, record before rendering

Packaging is not applied to a finished film; it is decided first and then written into the film.
Owner: [`skills/youtube-packaging/SKILL.md`](../skills/youtube-packaging/SKILL.md). Schema:
[`docs/production/CREATIVE_PACKAGING.md`](../docs/production/CREATIVE_PACKAGING.md) §3.

**The promise, in one sentence:** {{THE_PROMISE}} — complete the sentence *"I clicked because I
wanted to know ___."* Nothing starts until this exists.

1. **Hook candidates — at least 3, different angles, not rewordings.** Record all of them with the
   reason the chosen one won and what it cost. The chosen hook must land inside 8 seconds and its
   words must be the words actually spoken. Banned openers: "Have you ever wondered", "In this
   video", "Today we're going to", "Welcome back".
2. **Retention map — at least 4 beats** (hook → escalation → reveal → payoff), each with a stated
   purpose and a real timestamp. Any stretch over ~20 s with nothing new for the viewer is cut or
   given a reveal.
3. **Title candidates — at least 3 approaches** (curiosity, question, outcome/number,
   contradiction). One selected. It must be true to the film, and any number in it must match what
   the film says on screen and in narration.
4. **Thumbnail concepts — at least 3, each with a different focal subject.** Then generate base art
   separately in the film's visual language **with no lettering**, and typeset with
   [`tools/make_thumbnail.py`](../tools/make_thumbnail.py). The cover must complement the title,
   never repeat it, and must be checked at 168 px — the phone search size.
5. **Alignment statement:** how the title's promise, the cover's promise and the hook's promise are
   the same promise. Verdict `aligned` or the film is not ready.
6. **Claim labels:** every factual or predictive statement is `[M]` measured, `[O]` observed or
   `[P]` predicted, and a prediction is never used as a fact. **No CTR, retention or view number may
   be invented — there is no analytics access.**
7. **Script critique:** score all ten criteria 1–5, name the weakest, and record what the critique
   actually changed. A flat sheet means the script was not read critically.

Gate: `python3 tools/creative_gate.py` must pass before the master is rendered.

See [`skills/stickman-animation/SKILL.md`](../skills/stickman-animation/SKILL.md).

| id | Name | Role | build | hair | colour | posture | scale | accessories | expression arc |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

**Hard constraint:** never more than two characters in any scene.

## 5. Animation and visual style

- Style {{cel|parchment}}; zero film grain; 30 fps.
- Movement uses only the 60 supported actions in
  [`universal_toolbook/engine/motion_library.js`](../universal_toolbook/engine/motion_library.js).
  **No scene may rely on a static pose plus a zoom.**
- Camera: speech-locked `camera_shots` with multi-word `cue_on`; verify at the cue time in a draft.
- Information uses supported boards/props in
  [`universal_toolbook/engine/world_props_and_boards.js`](../universal_toolbook/engine/world_props_and_boards.js).
  If a primitive is missing, substitute an existing one and log it, or extend the engine reusably.
- Transitions, captions, timing and the real renderer map:
  [`skills/animation-production/references/toolbook-renderer-map.md`](../skills/animation-production/references/toolbook-renderer-map.md)
  and [`skills/animation-production/references/frame-based-animation.md`](../skills/animation-production/references/frame-based-animation.md).
- Remotion is **not** a rendering backend here; see
  [`docs/decisions/ADR-0001-remotion-evaluation.md`](../docs/decisions/ADR-0001-remotion-evaluation.md).

For every scene define: objective · characters · poses/actions · environment · camera · animation

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S01 | {{name}} | {{environment}} | {{objective}} | {{ids}} | {{actions}} | {{board/prop}} | {{segment}} | {{sfx}} | {{cut/fade}} |

After `episode.json`, run `python3 tools/make_scene_plan.py projects/{{SLUG}}` so `SCENE_PLAN.json`
is derived from the spec rather than duplicated by hand.

## 7. Narration voice and settings

| Speaker | Engine | Voice | Rate | Pitch | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| narrator | Kokoro | `am_michael` | +1% | −1 Hz | repository PRIMARY default |
| {{char}} | Kokoro | {{voice}} | {{rate}} | {{pitch}} | {{why}} |

- `af_bella` is the preferred secondary voice; other Kokoro voices only when they genuinely suit
  a character; Piper is fallback only. Never change these defaults silently.
- Configuration: [`universal_toolbook/tts/config/voices.json`](../universal_toolbook/tts/config/voices.json).
- Polish with [`docs/production/prompts/VOICEOVER_POLISH_PROMPT.md`](../docs/production/prompts/VOICEOVER_POLISH_PROMPT.md)
  **exactly as it exists, byte-for-byte**. Save `SCRIPT_ORIGINAL.md`, `SCRIPT_POLISHED.md`,
  `SCRIPT_CHANGELOG.md` (per change: line touched + justifying rule).
- After approval copy the polished text verbatim into `episode.json`. No editing between approval
  and render. Procedure: [`skills/scriptwriting/SKILL.md`](../skills/scriptwriting/SKILL.md).

## 8. Audio requirements

- BGM mode `dynamic`, per-scene tracks from
  [`universal_toolbook/assets/bgm/BGM_CATALOG.json`](../universal_toolbook/assets/bgm/BGM_CATALOG.json).
  Act mapping: {{ACT_MAP}}.
- Speech ducking on; narration clearly above music and effects; foley from scene events.
- **Measured targets on the rendered WAV:** peak −3…−1 dBFS, RMS −16…−19 dBFS. The engine
  normalises loudness (KI-008/PC-010). If a master still measures outside the band, fix the engine
  and re-render — never tweak one video's gains by hand.
- Record licence and attribution of every track in `ASSET_MANIFEST.json`.
- Procedure: [`skills/voiceover-audio/SKILL.md`](../skills/voiceover-audio/SKILL.md).

## 9. Export settings

| | Primary | Secondary |
|---|---|---|
| Profile | {{YouTube Shorts 9:16 \| Regular YouTube 16:9}} | {{the other}} |
| Resolution | {{1080×1920 \| 1920×1080}} | {{the other}} |
| Frame rate | 30 fps | 30 fps |
| Codec | H.264 High + AAC 44.1 kHz stereo | same |
| Preset / CRF | `veryfast` / `crf 24` | same |
| CLI flag | {{--shorts \| --aspect-ratio 9:16 \| --aspect-ratio 16:9}} | the other |
| Workers / chunk | 2 / 45 s, `--resume` on | same |
| Output | `projects/{{SLUG}}/final.mp4` | `projects/{{SLUG}}/renders/<name>.mp4` |

Keep important visuals in mobile-safe areas; inspect portrait stills before the master render.
Do not hand-author `portrait_focus` / `portrait_focus_x` / `portrait_w` / `portrait_x` as a first
instinct (KI-009): the engine auto-focuses the active character and re-fits boards. Overrides are
a last resort backed by a specific draft frame. Stills have no TTS timings, so cue-locked boards
must be judged from draft/master frames at `board_pop + ~1.6 s` (KI-003).

Multi-line `notebook_page` / `sketch_card` / `checklist_card` boards in 9:16 need explicit
geometry: `h>=250`, `y~74`, fixed 42-pixel line spacing, plus `portrait_w:460` and
`portrait_x:0.5` so `fitBoardToPortraitViewport` scales and centres the card and keeps the name
tag clear. After any such edit, inspect the **final-master** board-cue frames, not only the
draft: `--resume` caches must be invalidated (KI-011). See PC-010 / PC-012.

The 9:16 crop pans with the camera, so world props can drift into the frame edge. The renderer
prunes `signpost` label plates that would appear as clipped, unreadable fragments (KI-012), but
QA must still open the **closing** master frames after the last camera push: a prop that was
off-screen in a still can become visible there. Landscape masters use the full stage and are
unchanged by that guard.

## 9b. Publishing package (required for delivery)

A finished master is not a deliverable until it is a complete YouTube publishing package:

```
videos/{{SLUG}}/
├── {{SLUG}}.mp4     # master filename == directory slug; never final.mp4
├── script.md        # final approved script — retained permanently
├── thumbnail.jpg    # designed (not a frame grab): 1280x720 16:9 or 1080x1920 9:16, <2 MB
└── record.json      # title, full description, pinned comment, technical metadata
```

Plus one compact entry in `videos/index.json` (id, title, slug, topic, summary, key angle,
duration, format, produced date, directory, content fingerprint).

- **Title** — curiosity + clarity, natural to read, true to the film, no clickbait, no keyword
  stuffing, no emoji. Generate candidates internally; only the selected title is kept.
- **Thumbnail** — concept distinct from an ordinary scene, strong silhouette, readable at phone
  size, minimal text only when it improves the concept. Inspect the generated image, re-check
  spelling, re-check at small size, regenerate if wrong. It must represent the film truthfully.
- **Description** — written for viewers: opening, premise, reason to watch, real search terms,
  hashtags, CTA, verified music/asset credits. No invented links or unverified credits.
- **Pinned comment** — one genuine question tied to the film's central idea, inviting real
  experience. Never "like, subscribe and comment".
- **Gates, in order:**
  ```bash
  python3 tools/creative_gate.py
  python3 tools/thumbnail_copy.py
  python3 tools/thumbnail_style.py check videos/{{SLUG}}/{{SLUG}}.mp4 videos/{{SLUG}}/thumbnail.jpg --package videos/{{SLUG}}
  python3 tools/seo_audit.py --min 85
  python3 tools/validate_publishing.py
  ```
  All must print `PASS`. A passing gate proves the process ran; it does not prove the cover will
  earn a click. Look at the cover and the film together before publishing.

## 10. Quality requirements — all must actually pass, with evidence

1. `validate` reports `warnings: []` before any render.
2. Portrait (and landscape, if delivered) stills inspected for every scene: key visuals readable,
   boards inside the safe crop, no name-tag collision, no clipped limbs. After any board/geometry
   edit, repeat the check on final-master board-cue frames; a corrected draft is not enough.
   Also open the closing/end master frames for clipped world-prop labels or other edge fragments.
3. Draft render reviewed for timing, board build, camera cuts, subtitle speaker and highlight.
4. Master decodes end-to-end: `ffmpeg -v error -i final.mp4 -f null -` exits clean.
5. Measured container matches spec: dimensions, fps, duration, one video + one audio stream.
6. **No black-screen sections** — sampled frames across the timeline are non-uniform.
7. Audio measured on the mixed WAV: peak and RMS inside target, no unintended interior silence.
8. Frames extracted and **actually looked at** at ≥6 timestamps; findings in `QA_REPORT.md`.
9. Mute-legibility test: the extracted frame sequence tells the story without audio.
10. `tools/validate_structure.py`, `tests/` and CI-relevant checks pass.
11. `tools/validate_publishing.py` prints `PASS` for the delivered package.

**Never claim a visual or audio check passed if it was not performed.** Full gate:
[`skills/production-quality/SKILL.md`](../skills/production-quality/SKILL.md).

Create the project with `python3 scripts/new_project.py {{SLUG}} --title "{{TITLE}}"`.

## 12. Self-healing obligation

Any failure is recorded in `PRODUCTION_LOG.md`, root-caused, fixed **reusably**, covered by a
regression check in `tests/`, and written up in
[`docs/production/KNOWN_ISSUES.md`](../docs/production/KNOWN_ISSUES.md),
[`LESSONS_LEARNED.md`](../docs/production/LESSONS_LEARNED.md),
[`PIPELINE_CHANGELOG.md`](../docs/production/PIPELINE_CHANGELOG.md) and `CHANGELOG.md`.
A failure is never reported resolved without verification. Recurring problems are never hidden.

## 13. Delivery report

Provide: final MP4 · title and selected topic · original and polished scripts · preview/thumbnail
where supported · project folder and downloadable archive · production and QA report · test and CI
results · remaining limitations.
